/-!
# Erdős Problem 1071

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/1071](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1071)
* [Da85] Danzer, L., _Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry_.
  Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985), 167-177.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set Metric EuclideanGeometry Order

namespace Erdos1071

/-- Two segments are disjoint if they only intersect at their endpoints (if at all). -/
def SegmentsDisjoint (seg1 seg2 : ℝ² × ℝ²) : Prop :=
  segment ℝ seg1.1 seg1.2 ∩ segment ℝ seg2.1 seg2.2 ⊆ {seg1.1, seg1.2, seg2.1, seg2.2}

/--
Can a finite set of disjoint unit segments in a unit square be maximal?
Solved affirmatively by [Da85], who gave an explicit construction.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1071.lean"]
theorem erdos_1071.parts.i :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ S : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²),
      Maximal (fun T : Finset (ℝ² × ℝ²) =>
        (∀ seg ∈ T, dist seg.1 seg.2 = 1 ∧
          seg.1 0 ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ seg.1 1 ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧
          seg.2 0 ∈ Icc 0 1 ∧ seg.2 1 ∈ Icc 0 1) ∧
          (T : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²)).Pairwise SegmentsDisjoint) S := by
  sorry

/-- Is there a region $R$ with a maximal set of disjoint unit line segments that is countably infinite?
Here a unit line segment is a rotated and translated copy of the open interval $(0,1)$, and it is
required to be contained in $R$.
Solved affirmatively by [Fo99], who gave an explicit construction.

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev using Aristotle and ChatGPT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos1071b.lean"]
theorem erdos_1071.parts.ii :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ (R : Set ℝ²) (S : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²)),
      IsOpen R ∧ IsConnected R ∧ S.Countable ∧ S.Infinite ∧
      Maximal (fun T : Set (ℝ² × ℝ²) =>
        (∀ seg ∈ T, dist seg.1 seg.2 = 1 ∧ openSegment ℝ seg.1 seg.2 ⊆ R) ∧
        T.Pairwise SegmentsDisjoint) S := by
  sorry

end Erdos1071

findings.description: The bibliography attributes “Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry”, pp. 167–177, to L. Danzer under [Da85]. This article is by P. Erdős and was published in 1987 in the proceedings of the 1985 Siófok meeting. Danzer supplied the finite construction reported in the article; he is not its author. The mathematical statements are unaffected.

reformulations.difference: The source requires disjoint open unit segments. Lean instead requires the intersection of the closed segments to lie in the union of their four endpoints. In particular, it permits an endpoint of one closed segment to lie inside the other.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Unit length implies that each segment has distinct endpoints. Its open segment is therefore its closed segment with the two endpoints removed. A point belongs to both open segments exactly when it belongs to both closed segments and is none of the four endpoints. Consequently the subset condition is precisely disjointness of the open segments. This does not encode the separate, stronger closed-segment variant mentioned in the source’s remarks. The exact equivalence was proved as Review1071.segmentsDisjoint_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Maximality is tested only against finite families, and containment in the unit square is expressed by coordinate bounds on the endpoints rather than containment of the open segments.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Admissibility is hereditary. If any larger admissible family existed, adding just one of its new segments would give a larger admissible finite family, so finite-family maximality is equivalent to unrestricted inclusion maximality. Also, the closed unit square is convex and closed: endpoints in it imply that the whole segment lies in it, while an open segment contained in it has its endpoints in it by closure. Both equivalences were proved in the scratch files (maximal_finset_iff_set and endpoints_iff_openSegment_subset).
